citations.quote: **Primary lung squamous cell carcinoma**, moderately differentiated, left upper lobe

candidates.description: The histological classification of the lung primary tumor.
candidates.extraction_instruction: Identify the diagnosis in the pathology report; assign 'Squamous cell carcinoma' if the diagnosis is squamous cell carcinoma and 'Adenocarcinoma' if the diagnosis is adenocarcinoma.
candidates.measurement_definition: Determined by microscopic evaluation and immunohistochemistry (IHC) markers; squamous cell carcinoma is characterized by p40 positivity and TTF-1 negativity, while adenocarcinoma is characterized by TTF-1 and Napsin A positivity and p40 negativity.
candidates.name: NSCLC Histologic Subtype
candidates.uncertainty: None; the distinction is clearly defined by pathology reports.

candidates.description: The Tumor Proportion Score (TPS) of PD-L1 expression in the tumor cells.
candidates.extraction_instruction: Extract the numerical percentage value associated with PD-L1 Tumor Proportion Score (TPS).
candidates.measurement_definition: Percentage of viable tumor cells showing partial or complete membrane staining for PD-L1 as determined by immunohistochemistry (e.g., using the 22C3 clone).
candidates.name: PD-L1 Expression (TPS)
candidates.uncertainty: The exact IHC clone used may vary across patients (e.g., 22C3 mentioned for one patient).

limitations: Small sample size of patients provided in the evidence.
Lack of variability in ECOG performance status (mostly ECOG 2) makes it a poor candidate for this discovery task.
summary: The evidence identifies distinct histological subtypes of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), specifically squamous cell carcinoma and adenocarcinoma, and provides quantitative measurements of PD-L1 expression (TPS).
